A 62-year-old female presents with progressive bilateral lower leg numbness over 5 months, initially
affecting her toes and advancing to her ankles and calves. She reports nocturnal tingling sensations in
her feet that disturb her sleep, and recent clumsiness in her hands. Her medical history includes a brief
vegan diet last year for weight loss, but is otherwise unremarkable. She takes no medications and
hasn't had regular medical care. Physical examination reveals: height 168 cm, weight 89 kg (BMI 32
kg/m2), temperature 37.0°C, pulse 76/min, respirations 15/min, and blood pressure 155/92 mm Hg.
Neurological examination shows decreased muscle strength (4/5) in the lower legs, diminished deep
tendon reflexes in lower extremities (1+) compared to upper extremities (2+), and reduced pinprick and
vibration sensation throughout the lower extremities. Which diagnostic test would be most appropriate
to determine the underlying cause of her symptoms? Answer Choices: (A) Serum folate level
measurement (B) Thyroid function tests (C) Lumbar puncture for CSF analysis (D) Genetic testing for
hereditary neuropathy (E) Anti-ganglioside antibody testing (F) Measurement of hemoglobin A1c (G)
Anti-MAG antibody testing (H) Nerve conduction studies (I) Measurement of vitamin B12 concentration
(J) Serum protein electrophoresis
 A. Serum protein electrophoresis
B. Nerve conduction studies
C. Anti-ganglioside antibody testing
D. Lumbar puncture for CSF analysis

F. Thyroid function tests
G. Measurement of hemoglobin A1c
H. Serum folate level measurement
